setup.title: Connect & configure
setup.subtitle: Use the same Sentry project for event capture, issue access and build artifacts.
setup.tokenNotice: The read token stays on the server and needs event:read and project:read. Keep the source-map upload token separate; never use a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix for either token.

project.title: Choose the project
project.body: Copy the DSN from Sentry project settings. Use organization and project slugs from the URL, and confirm the US or EU data region.

runtime.title: Enable capture for your environment
runtime.body: Set the public DSN and environment label. Monitoring defaults to production; enable it explicitly only when you intend to capture local or staging events.

readToken.title: Add dedicated issue access
readToken.body: Create a server-only token with event:read and project:read for this project. Set it as SENTRY_READ_AUTH_TOKEN with the organization and project slugs.

deploy.title: Rebuild, deploy & verify
deploy.body: Public settings require a new build. Refresh the inbox after deployment, then verify ingestion, source frames and alert delivery in the intended Sentry environment.

setup.buildBody: Provide the upload token only to CI or the build step, together with the organization, project and an immutable release ID. Match the SDK's release ID to the build. Set SENTRY_UPLOAD_SOURCE_MAPS=false for verification builds.
setup.buildVerify: Check the build upload result and the matching artifact bundle in Sentry. A configured status does not prove upload success; unverified is expected when the build token is absent from runtime.

workflow.title: From issue to verified fix
workflow.subtitle: A repeatable workflow for investigating failures and confirming the repair in production.

triage.title: 1. Triage the impact
triage.body: Choose the affected environment. Review severity, recent occurrence, reported event counts and affected users. Confirm the issue belongs to the release you are investigating.

inspect.title: 2. Read the event
inspect.body: Open the full Sentry issue and start with the first application stack frame. Inspect the release, trace and masked replay when available to understand the failing flow.

reproduce.title: 3. Reproduce the failure
reproduce.body: Check out the event's release and use test data to repeat the affected steps. Correlate the operation and opaque request or job ID with your application logs.

repair.title: 4. Fix & test
repair.body: Repair the underlying code or configuration. Add a regression test that reproduces the failure, then run the relevant checks and verify the affected flow.

release.title: 5. Deploy an identifiable release
release.body: Deploy the fix with a unique release ID and matching source maps. Check upload results and confirm the affected flow works in the intended environment.

verify.title: 6. Resolve & watch
verify.body: After verifying the repair, resolve the issue in Sentry, or resolve it in the fixed release. Watch new and regressed issues and confirm production alerts reach the right owner.

workflow.resolveNotice: Marking an issue resolved does not change application code. Verify the deployed fix before resolving it, and investigate if the issue returns.

troubleshooting.title: Common questions
troubleshooting.subtitle: Checks that help when issues, source frames or monitoring signals are missing.

noIssues.title: Why is the inbox empty?
noIssues.body: Clear local search, select all environments and widen the period. Check unresolved, resolved and ignored statuses. Then verify the deployed DSN, enabled setting and environment. A connected inbox proves read access, not error ingestion.

access.title: Why can I not open an issue?
access.body: The app requires an administrator session. Sentry requires its own sign-in and access to the configured organization and project. For API access failures, check the runtime read token, event:read/project:read permissions and organization region.

sourceMaps.title: Why are stack traces minified?
sourceMaps.body: Compare the event release with the deployed build. Check CI source-map uploads and the matching artifact bundle in Sentry. Uploads need build-only credentials; adding that token to runtime does not repair missing artifacts.

missingReplay.title: Why is there no trace or replay?
missingReplay.body: Sampling means some events have neither. Confirm the browser DSN, enabled setting and sampling rates, then check Sentry plan limits and browser network restrictions. Server-only errors may have no associated browser session.

noise.title: How do I reduce alert noise?
noise.body: Scope alerts to production, assign owners and choose useful thresholds. Review grouping and repeated failures before changing rules. Tune trace and replay sampling for traffic and quota; those rates do not sample error reporting.

regression.title: What if a resolved issue returns?
regression.body: Compare the new event's release and stack frames with the verified fix. Check whether every deployment received the change and whether a new input triggers the same failure. Reproduce it, extend the regression test and deploy the repair.
